The test image shows a cut stem segment in a glass beaker of water with white milky bacterial ooze streaming down from the cut end — this is the classic "streaming test" for bacterial wilt. The stem also shows brown vascular discoloration. This strongly points to **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**.

Now I'll read reference images across 8 different classes.

Bugwood_3.jpg is essentially identical to the test image — same streaming test setup, same bacterial ooze streaming from cut stem, same brown vascular discoloration. This strongly matches **Bacterial_Wilt**. Let me now check 5 more classes.

The evidence is clear. The test image (ID 5606065) is nearly identical to `Bacterial_Wilt/stem/Bugwood_3.jpg` (ID 5606063) — same glass beaker streaming test, same white milky bacterial ooze streaming downward from the cut stem, same brown vascular discoloration in the stem interior. Both are from the same Bugwood photo series (IDs 5606059, 5606063, 5606065). The other classes (Verticillium_Wilt, Early_Blight, Late_Blight, Septoria, Powdery_Mildew, Gray_Mold, Bacterial_Canker) all show leaf or stem field symptoms that look nothing like this diagnostic beaker setup.
